10 Two train carriages each of mass 5000 kg roll toward one another on a horizontal frictionless
track. One is travelling at a speed of 2.00 m s–1 and the other at a speed of 1.00 m s–1, as shown.
2.00 m s–1
1.00 m s–1
5000 kg
5000 kg
They collide and join together.
What is the kinetic energy lost during the collision?
A
1250 J
B
7500 J
C
11 250 J
D
12 500 J

hints: Notice the opposite velocities of the two $5000 \text{ kg}$ carriages: take right as positive so the momenta are $+5000 \times 2.00$ and $-5000 \times 1.00$ in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$.
Because they join together, use conservation of total momentum to find the single final velocity of the $10000 \text{ kg}$ combined mass.
Calculate total kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ before and after separately, then subtract final from initial to get the loss in $\text{J}$.
walkthrough: Take right as positive. Total momentum before is $p = 5000 \times 2.00 + 5000 \times (-1.00) = 10000 - 5000 = 5000 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
After joining, total mass is $M = 5000 + 5000 = 10000 \text{ kg}$. By momentum conservation, $Mv = 5000$, so $v = 5000/10000 = 0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the right.
Initial kinetic energy is the sum of both: $E_{k1} = \frac{1}{2} \times 5000 \times (2.00)^2 + \frac{1}{2} \times 5000 \times (1.00)^2 = 10000 + 2500 = 12500 \text{ J}$.
Final kinetic energy of the joined carriages is $E_{k2} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10000 \times (0.50)^2 = 5000 \times 0.25 = 1250 \text{ J}$.
Energy lost as heat, sound and deformation is $E_{k1} - E_{k2} = 12500 - 1250 = 11250 \text{ J}$. This is option C

A.explanation: This is the kinetic energy after joining, $1250 \text{ J}$, not the energy lost. Loss is initial minus final.

B.explanation: This value is too small and does not follow from momentum conservation with $5000 \text{ kg}$, $2.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $1.00 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: Initial total $12500 \text{ J}$ minus final $1250 \text{ J}$ gives $11250 \text{ J}$ lost in the inelastic joining.

D.explanation: This is the total initial kinetic energy, $10000 \text{ J} + 2500 \text{ J}$. It ignores the $1250 \text{ J}$ still carried by the joined mass.
